en: The Heart Sūtra of the Perfection of Wisdom [Extended Version]
Homage to the Omniscient One!
Thus have I heard.
At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Rājagṛha on Vulture Peak Mountain, together with a great saṅgha of bhikṣus and a great saṅgha of bodhisattvas.
At that time, the Blessed One had entered the samādhi called the Profound and Unfathomable Awakening.
And at that time, the noble Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, while practicing the course of the profound perfection of wisdom, looked down in this way;
he looked upon those five aggregates and saw that they were empty of intrinsic nature.

Then, through the power of the Buddha, the Venerable Śāriputra said this to the Bodhisattva Āryāvalokiteśvara: "If any son of good family or daughter of good family wishes to practice the course of this profound perfection of wisdom,
how should they train?"
When this had been said, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Āryāvalokiteśvara spoke thus to the venerable Śāriputra:

"Śāriputra, whatever son of good family or daughter of good family wishes to practice the course of this profound perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), they should observe in this way: they should perceive the five aggregates as empty of intrinsic nature."
Form is emptiness,
and emptiness itself is form.
Emptiness is not separate from form.
Form is not separate from emptiness;
whatever is form, that is emptiness, and whatever is emptiness, that is form.
In the same way, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness are emptiness.
Thus, Śāriputra, all dharmas have the characteristic of emptiness; they are unproduced and unceasing, neither defiled nor pure, neither deficient nor complete.
Therefore, Śāriputra, in emptiness there is no form.
It is not feeling, it is not perception, and it is not mental formations.
There is no consciousness, no eye, no ear, no nose, no tongue, no body, no mind; no form, no sound, no odor, no taste, no tangible object, and no mental phenomenon.
There is no eye-element, and so on, up to no mind-element, no mental-object-element, and no mind-consciousness-element.

There is no ignorance, nor non-ignorance; there is no destruction up to and including no old age and death, nor the destruction of old age and death; there is no suffering, no origin, no cessation, and no path; there is no knowledge, no attainment, and no non-attainment.
Therefore, Śāriputra, because of this non-attainment, bodhisattvas rely upon the perfection of wisdom.
He dwells with a mind free from hindrances;
because there are no hindrances to the mind, he is fearless, has transcended all perversions, and has reached the ultimate nirvana.
All Buddhas dwelling in the three times, by relying on the perfection of wisdom, have fully awakened to unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment.

Therefore, one should know that the Great Mantra of the Perfection of Wisdom is the unsurpassed mantra, the unequaled mantra, the mantra that allays all suffering; because it is true and not false, this mantra has been proclaimed in the Perfection of Wisdom. It is as follows: *gate gate pāragate pārasaṃgate bodhi svāhā*.
In this way, Śāriputra, a bodhisattva should train in the practice of the profound perfection of wisdom.
Then the Blessed One, having arisen from that samādhi, gave his approval to the Bodhisattva Āryāvalokiteśvara: "Excellent, excellent, noble son!
It is so, noble son; it is just as you have explained: this is how one should practice the course in the profound perfection of wisdom."
It is rejoiced in by the Tathāgatas, the Arhats.
Thus spoke the Blessed One.

The Venerable Śāriputra, the Bodhisattva Āryāvalokiteśvara, and that entire assembly, including the world with its gods, humans, asuras, and gandharvas, rejoiced in what the Blessed One had spoken. Thus ends the Heart Sūtra on the Perfection of Wisdom.
